name: Tata Consultancy Services (TCS)
overview: TCS is an Indian IT services and consulting company headquartered in Mumbai and part of the Tata Group. It works across 46 countries and is one of the largest private-sector employers in India. Most freshers join through the TCS National Qualifier Test (NQT).
variation_note: One NQT decides Ninja, Digital or Prime; section timings, cutoffs and interview rounds change by year, slot and campus.

roles.title: Assistant System Engineer Trainee (Ninja)
roles.description: Entry track for application development, maintenance, testing and support work. Given for clearing the NQT at the base cutoff.

eligibility.text: Minimum 60% or 6.0 CGPA in 10th, 12th, diploma, UG and PG
Maximum 1 active backlog at the time of the test, all cleared before joining (GfG)
No backlogs at the time of the selection process (PrepInsta; sources disagree, check the official notice)
Academic gap not more than 24 months

compensation.text: 3.36 LPA for UG, 3.53 LPA for PG (as reported)

roles.title: System Engineer (Digital)
roles.description: Higher track for development and newer technology work. Needs a higher NQT score and a tougher technical interview.

eligibility.text: Same academic criteria as Ninja; tagged by a higher NQT cutoff

compensation.text: 7.09 to 7.30 LPA for UG, 7.39 to 7.60 LPA for PG at 0 to 1 year (as reported)

roles.title: Prime
roles.description: Top track for AI, ML and next-generation technology work. Highest NQT cutoff and hardest interview, often with live coding.

eligibility.text: Same academic criteria; tagged by the highest NQT cutoff

compensation.text: 9.09 to 9.30 LPA for UG, 11.59 to 11.80 LPA for PG at 0 to 1 year (as reported)

stages.name: NQT Part A: Foundation section
stages.what: Mandatory first part of the NQT with numerical, verbal and reasoning questions. Taken at a TCS iON centre. No negative marking.

format.text: TCS NQT is one integrated test of 190 minutes with two mandatory parts (official hiring page, seen in search snippet)
65 questions in 75 minutes: Verbal 25, Reasoning 20, Quantitative 20
65 questions in 76 minutes: Numerical 20 (25 min), Verbal 25 (26 min), Reasoning 20 (25 min)
Verbal now has 20 sentence completion, 4 passage recall and 1 professional email writing task; non-adaptive, no negative marking

study: Time and work, speed and distance
tips: You cannot go back to a question once you move on, so answer before moving
No negative marking, so never leave a question blank
Calculator and rough pad are on screen; practise using them
stages.before_next: Finish timed mock tests of the full Foundation section at least twice.
stages.label: Third-party

stages.name: NQT Part B: Advanced quant and reasoning
stages.what: Harder quantitative and reasoning questions. Your score here, with coding, decides whether you are considered for Digital or Prime.
tips: Skip and guess fast on long DI sets; time is shared
Learn shortcut formulas for P&C and probability
stages.before_next: Practise 2 to 3 advanced aptitude sets with a 25 minute timer.
stages.label: Third-party

stages.name: NQT Part B: Advanced coding
stages.what: Write full programs for problem statements in a language of your choice. Input is read from standard input.

format.text: 2 questions in 90 minutes covering programming constructs, data structures and algorithms

tips: Read input exactly as the format says
Test edge cases like N=1 before submitting
Write the simple brute force first, then improve
stages.before_next: Solve the PrepInsta TCS NQT slot-wise coding questions in your main language.
stages.label: Third-party

stages.name: Technical interview
stages.what: Face-to-face or virtual round on programming basics, OOP, DBMS and your final-year project. Harder for Digital and Prime.

format.text: Deep dive into data structures, OOP, DBMS and final-year project
About 25 to 30 minutes, in person; questions on Python vs Java, DBMS JOIN with UPDATE (Digital, Jan 2026)

study: SQL joins and UPDATE with JOIN
tips: Say honestly when you do not know, then explain what you do know
Be ready to explain every tool written in your resume
stages.before_next: Prepare a 2-minute explanation of each project and revise SQL joins.
stages.label: Candidate-reported

stages.name: Managerial interview
stages.what: Questions on problem solving, situations, teamwork and project decisions.

format.text: Focus on problem-solving, situational judgment and project management
About 20 minutes; project, team lead role, metadata, false positive rate (Digital, Jan 2026)

study: Basic ML metrics if you have ML projects
stages.before_next: Write down 3 STAR stories from your college work.
stages.label: Candidate-reported

stages.name: HR interview
stages.what: Behaviour, communication, document check and questions on relocation and shifts.

format.text: Behavioural assessment, communication check, documents and relocation flexibility
Willing to relocate and work night shifts were asked (older Ninja report)

tips: Keep original documents and photocopies ready
stages.before_next: Keep marksheets, ID and NQT details ready for verification.
stages.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: Coding
questions.question: Given an array of N integers, count the elements that are greater than all elements before them. The first element always counts. Example: 7 4 8 2 9 gives 3.
questions.answer: Keep a running maximum; each time a value is greater than it, add 1 and update the maximum. [7,4,8,2,9] gives 3 and [3,4,5,8,9] gives 5 (checked in Python).
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: Coding
questions.question: A product code N is printed on each item. The price is the product of all digits of N. Example: 5244 gives 160.
questions.answer: Multiply the digits one by one: 5*2*4*4 = 160 (checked in Python).
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: Coding
questions.question: Given a positive integer N (1 to 100), toggle all bits of its binary form from the most significant bit down and print the new value. Example: 10 (1010) gives 5 (0101).
questions.answer: Build a mask of all 1s with the same bit length, mask = (1 << bit_length) - 1, and print N XOR mask. 10 XOR 15 = 5 (checked in Python).
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: Other
questions.question: What is the difference between a Python list and an array?
questions.answer: A list can hold mixed types and grows freely; an array (array module or NumPy) holds one type, uses less memory and is faster for numeric work.
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: Other
questions.question: Is Python a compiled or an interpreted language? Can Python code run on another system without an interpreter?
questions.answer: Python source is compiled to bytecode and then run by the Python interpreter (virtual machine), so it is usually called interpreted. It needs an interpreter on the other system unless it is packaged with one (for example PyInstaller).
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: SQL
questions.question: Write an UPDATE query that uses a JOIN, for example raise salary by 10% for employees in the 'Sales' department.
questions.answer: MySQL: UPDATE employee e JOIN department d ON e.dept_id = d.id SET e.salary = e.salary * 1.10 WHERE d.name = 'Sales'; (syntax differs by database).
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: Project
questions.question: What is false positive rate, and how do you think about it in a multi-class classification problem?
questions.answer: FPR = FP / (FP + TN). For multi-class you compute it per class (one class vs rest) and then average (macro or weighted).
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: Networks
questions.question: What is a subnet mask? What is the difference between TCP and UDP?
questions.answer: A subnet mask splits an IP address into network and host parts (for example 255.255.255.0). TCP is connection-based and reliable with ordering; UDP is connectionless, faster and has no delivery guarantee.
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: HR
questions.question: Are you willing to relocate and work in night shifts?
questions.answer: Answer honestly and positively, for example: yes, I am open to relocating and to shifts while I learn the project.
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: Logical
questions.question: Find the next number: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
questions.answer: 42. Differences are 4, 6, 8, 10, so the next difference is 12.
